harms.add: Cold storage protects food only when the cold holds from farm to market; equipment alone does not show fewer losses.

sources.label: UNEP and FAO, 2022: sustainable food cold chains

harms.add: Refrigeration adds emissions through the power it uses and the refrigerants that leak, set against the food losses it avoids.

sources.label: UNEP and FAO, 2022: sustainable food cold chains

harms.add: Less heat at work can protect output: in garment factories near Bengaluru, switching to LED lighting, which gives off less heat, softened the drop in output on hot days (one firm's rollout, analysed in a working paper).

sources.label: Adhvaryu et al., MIT CEEPR working paper, 2017: the light and the heat, productivity co-benefits of energy-saving technology

links: Food that rots carries an emissions cost of its own.
Where forest is cleared, outdoor workers face more heat and get less done.

watch.text: In laboratory trials with older adults, fans slightly cooled the body in hot, humid air but raised body temperature in very hot, dry air. These were short trials, not homes.

sources.label: Chaseling et al., 2025: older adults' responses to fan use in heat extremes (PMC12308431)

watch.text: A 2025 review found no study that measured health outcomes for people using cooling centres; in simulated heatwaves, the benefits were short-lived. That is not evidence of no benefit.

sources.label: Dearman et al., UKHSA, 2025: public health effectiveness of cooling centres, a systematic review

questions.q: Does cooling matched to local heat reduce strain in homes without adding bills people cannot afford?
questions.have: Short laboratory trials show fans help in some conditions and not others; there is no household evidence in the region.
questions.could: Compare supported cooling packages in occupied homes, with consent, health oversight and cost tracking.
questions.scale: Illustrative: about a hundred households in contrasting climates over one hot season

questions.q: Does pay-per-use cold storage cut food losses and leave producers better off after fees?
questions.have: A pilot in Muzaffarpur, India, offered pay-per-use storage; its outcomes have not been independently checked.
questions.could: Phase access in with comparison producers, temperature logs and accounts of what producers earn after fees.
questions.scale: Illustrative: a few hundred producers at four markets over two harvests

questions.q: How long does protection last after people leave a cooling space?
questions.have: A review found only short-lived benefits in simulations and no real-world health outcomes for users.
questions.could: Follow consenting users and similar non-users through the rest of hot days, measuring exposure and health.
questions.scale: Illustrative: about 150 people over six hot weeks
